To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transformation of Pseudomonus fluorescens with a seven-gene operons for phenazine-1- carboxylic acid synthesis improves biocontrol of Rhizoctonia solani and in situ antibiotic biosynthesis.

a recombinant strain of P. fluorescens Q2-87 was created that produces both phenazine-1- carboxylic acid and 2,4- diacetylphloroglucionol and that this strain suppresses Rhizoctonia solani, the causative agent of rhizoctonai root rot, at a dose 1 to 2 orders of magnitude lower (10(2) cfu per seed) than the dose of the parental strain required
a recombinant pseudomonad that produces two antifungal compounds is more suppressive of Rhizoctonia than a strain that produces a single compound.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biocontrol agents that are based on the use of plant-associated bacteria.
the development of new biocontrol agents and with the elucidation of the molecular basis of biological control of plant diseases.
the development of a new biofungicide for the control of root rot disease of wheat, and the development of a method to produce the biofungicide in situ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of the phenazine-1- carboxylic acid operon to Pseudomonas fluorescence Q8r1 -96 improved its biocontrol of Rhizoctonia but not of Pythium or take-all.
phenazine production by P. fluorescens is not essential for take-all disease suppression, but does contribute to disease suppression of Rhizoctonia.
phenazine-1carboxylic acid production by Pseudomonas spp. has a positive effect in the biocontrol of rhizophagous fungi, but not on take-all of wheat or Pythium spp. root rot.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of a gene for phenazine synthesis did not improve biocontrol of take-all, but did improve biocontrol of Rhizoctonia and in situ antibiotic synthesis.

the addition of a single antifungal metabolite to a strain with an established capacity for root colonization and biocontrol can improve disease suppression, and that the combination of two antifungal compounds can improve disease suppression further.

the introduction of a gene cluster for phenazine production into a strain with an existing antifungal compound (phloroglucine) improved the strain's ability to suppress a soilborne pathogen, Rhizoctonia solani, but had no impact on its ability to suppress two other soilborne pathogens, Pythium ultimum and Gaeumannomyces graminis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

P. fluorescens Q2-87, a biocontrol strain of P. fluorescences that produces the antifungal metabolite 2,4 diacetylphloroglucionol, can be genetically engineered to produce the additional metabolite phenazine-1 carboxylic acid and thus be improved as a biological agent for the control of Rhizoctonia solani, a soilborne pathogen of many crop plants.
